# Wall-time budgets in seconds, one row per labeled verification stage.
# Linux columns name CPU classes mapped below to exact /proc/cpuinfo model
# names. Each stage/class budget is 1.1 times the maximum of at least its 20 most
# recent recorded runs (the newest 50 when there are more), plus that maximum's
# distance above the median of those runs, rounded up to 5 s, with a 10 s
# floor. A class whose runs vary little keeps a margin near 10%; a class
# seen to vary gets that variation on top, so one run on a slow host does not
# turn the gate red while a stage that has really slowed does. The 10 s floor
# is older than the 2026-10-13 ruling and can affect only stages whose measured
# maximum is below about 9 s. .github/recompute-time-budgets.py applies the rule
# to the stage times in CI logs; the gate.yml rows were last recomputed on
# 2026-11-25 over the newest 50 runs of each stage and class (a class that
# follows the rule had 20 to 50 of them; research/investigations/test-economy/
# time-budgets.md, "The margin of the budget rule"). The rows of the other
# workflows (io-hosts, proof, sanitizers, map-sanitizers, compute-regression)
# were not recomputed, except performance-candidate-compiler (below): the newest
# runs collected of them on 2026-11-26 give no class 20 samples of a stage, and
# the logs of all but sanitizers name no CPU model, so a run cannot be given a
# class. Each of those holds the value it had under
# the former rule, a fixed 10% over the maximum, or the provisional value noted
# at it, raised by a tenth, rounded up to 5 s, in the owner's raise of
# 2026-11-25 (cells at the 10 s floor were not raised). A cell with fewer than
# 20 runs of its class keeps its value, except in a column the owner added (see
# xeon-8573c and xeon-6975p below).
# A model with fewer than 20 runs has no column unless the owner adds one. An
# unmapped model uses the stage's largest Linux class budget and is reported by
# name. Unsampled rows
# retain the former Linux values until per-CPU runs are recorded in
# research/investigations/test-economy/time-budgets.md.
#
# macos values remain reported references: overruns are report-only, and so are
# the stages named in WHITEFOOT_BUDGET_REPORT_ONLY (see AGENTS.md "Checks").
# Linux and Windows overruns fail the final CI verdict; a missing row for the host fails
# on every host. run-check.pl preserves the command's status and records these
# results when WHITEFOOT_TIME_BUDGET_RECORD is set. Without a record it prints
# the comparison only. "-" marks a stage that does not run on that host.
# Windows values retain their existing rule: 1.25 times the recorded maximum,
# rounded up to 5 s, with a 10 s floor, or an owner-set value. AGENTS.md "Checks"
# states how to judge an overrun; budget raises need the owner's decision.
# Windows raises keep the 10 s increment for the stage and its group, if any.

cpu epyc-7763  AMD EPYC 7763 64-Core Processor
cpu epyc-9v74  AMD EPYC 9V74 80-Core Processor
cpu epyc-9v45  AMD EPYC 9V45 96-Core Processor
# xeon-8573c was added by the owner on 2026-10-13 with fewer than the 20 runs a
# class needs. A row with 20 or more runs on this CPU follows the rule like any
# class, recomputed with .github/recompute-time-budgets.py. With fewer, the
# value is the larger of the row's largest recomputed class value and, where a
# run on this CPU was found, that run's budget by the rule above (one
# compute-regression run for the compute rows, 13 and 8 runs for the two
# sanitizer programs rows, none for the others). Only
# performance-baseline-compiler rises above the largest class. Evidence:
# research/investigations/test-economy/time-budgets.md.
# performance-candidate-compiler was recomputed on 2026-11-26 by the rule above
# over the cold builds of the candidate compiler sampled for item 289 after the
# untimed toolchain warm-up (24, 29 and 23 runs on the three EPYC classes, 23 on
# xeon-6975p, 12 on this CPU; research/investigations/test-economy/
# time-budgets.md, "The first compiler build's extra time"). The owner had set it
# per class (165 s on epyc-7763, 150 s on epyc-9v74, 135 s on epyc-9v45) from runs
# made without the warm-up, whose first build took about 7% longer than a second.
# Its xeon-8573c cell is the largest class, 185 s, its own 12 runs giving 170 s.
cpu xeon-8573c INTEL(R) XEON(R) PLATINUM 8573C
# xeon-6975p was added on 2026-11-25 (item 289): the hosted pool had moved to
# this model, 16 of the 36 jobs of one experiment and 50 of the 80 of two
# sampling batches, and without a column it took each row's largest class value.
# It follows the rule of xeon-8573c above. Until a row has 20 runs on this CPU,
# its value is the larger of the row's largest recomputed class value and, where
# a run on this CPU was found, that run's budget by the rule above. Every row
# other than performance-candidate-compiler started at the largest of its Linux
# cells before the column existed, which is the value an unmapped model had.
# performance-candidate-compiler has 23 runs on this CPU and follows the rule
# like a class.
cpu xeon-6975p Intel(R) Xeon(R) 6975P-C

label                           epyc-7763  epyc-9v74  epyc-9v45  xeon-8573c  xeon-6975p  macos  windows

# gate.yml, Linux parts of the unit and corpus groups (shard-tests.pl): each
# part builds for itself and runs a share of the group's tests, so a part
# cannot take longer than the whole group, and each CPU column starts at the
# whole group's row above. Once a class has 20 runs of a part, the rule above
# recomputes its row. macOS runs each group whole, under the rows above.

compiler/test-unit-shard        220        235        140        205         235         -      -

# over the conformance cases. Provisional until 20 runs are recorded: 1.5 times

# compute-regression.yml: the candidate's cold compiler build and, unless the
# merge-base compiler is restored from the cache of its main commit, that
# build, at two Cargo jobs; their images, the instrument's slowdown and placement
# controls with the shifted images the latter builds, and the judgment of each
# kernel whose two images differ: its null control and the paired comparison,
# and, for a kernel the comparison failed while its own null control read at
# the threshold, a retest round of the two. A stage that has no kernel to time
# does not run and records nothing; the retest rows have the budget of the
# round they repeat, five kernels at the most.

performance-baseline-compiler   130        130        130        150         150         -      -

performance-baseline-images     10         10         10         10          10          -      -

performance-slow-control        65         65         65         65          65          -      -

performance-comparison          50         50         50         50          50          -      -
performance-retest-null         50         50         50         50          50          -      -
performance-retest-comparison   50         50         50         50          50          -      -

# compute-regression.yml, the data-placement control (tests/performance/
# data-placement.sh): one record of both arms' mapping calls, and one round of
# one kernel, both arms at the 32 positions; a run executes the record once
# and, with the qualification, three times, and each kernel's round up to four
# times. Each cell is the rule above, 1.1 times the maximum plus its distance
# above the median, over every run of that label on its model that the logs
# hold: the control's confirmation, the run that confirmed the judgment's
# reading of its list and three runs of compute-regression.yml by hand. The
# three EPYC classes have 7 to 32 runs a cell, fewer than the rule asks;
# xeon-6975p has 42 runs of each round and 104 of the record, and follows the
# rule like a class; xeon-8573c, which none of them reached, takes the row's
# largest class value
# (research/investigations/data-placement/README.md, "Confirmation"). A kernel
# added to the instrument needs its round's row.
performance-data-layout         10         10         10         10          10          -      -
performance-data-round-mandelbrot 15       25         15         25          15          -      -
performance-data-round-records  15         20         15         20          15          -      -
performance-data-round-fir      15         20         10         20          10          -      -
performance-data-round-quadrature 15       15         10         15          10          -      -
performance-data-round-stencil  65         80         45         80          45          -      -
